confirmed_issues.claim_in_catalog: Title: "Resume paused or interrupted work"; summary: "Continue the same durable run after a checkpoint, interruption, or host restart."
confirmed_issues.what_is_wrong: Resume only continues runs parked at a declared checkpoint (including across host restarts, since the parked run folder is durable). A run interrupted before reaching a checkpoint cannot be resumed at all: `circuit resume` refuses it with exit 2 and points the operator at `circuit runs show`. The title and summary claim interruption recovery as shipped scope; mid-run crash recovery is not shipped (it is a separate, unmerged durability workstream), and the only crash-adjacent resume path is a checkpoint whose trace tail was torn during parking. `--reuse-children-from` explicitly starts a fresh run, not the same durable run. A reader would conclude in-flight interruption recovery is shipped and could deprioritize crash-durability work based on this entry.

confirmed_candidates.title: Crash salvage via --reuse-children-from is a recovery grain the catalog does not carry
confirmed_candidates.detail: A fresh run can reuse the finished fanout branches of a prior crashed run's folder by structural address instead of re-running them (`--reuse-children-from <path>`, fresh-run only, rejected on resume). This is materially different from both resume-work (same durable run continues) and recover-cleanly (reclaim orphaned resources): it salvages completed work product across run identities, i.e. restart cheapness. It belongs in the continuity area, likely as an extension relationship on recover-cleanly or resume-work.

verdict.reasoning: All factual claims verified on main: --reuse-children-from is committed (c45b46b5), fresh-run only with an explicit resume rejection (src/cli/run.ts:407-409), reuses finished sub-run fanout branches of a prior crashed run's folder by structural address (step_id, branch_id) without resuming the dead run (src/runtime/run/reuse-children.ts header), is publicly documented in CLI help (src/cli/help.ts:103-104), tested (tests/runtime/reuse-children.test.ts), and surfaces in the run contract (docs/contracts/run.md:144 'reused_from'). The grain objection partially lands (it is a run flag, and the catalog doesn't map flags), but unlike --tournament/--autonomous/--power this flag's outcome has no capability whose summary covers it, so the omission is a semantic hole rather than flag-grain noise; low severity and extension-relationship placement are appropriate. Sharpened: the host should be recover-cleanly, not resume-work.
verdict.correction: Crash salvage via --reuse-children-from is a shipped, tested, publicly documented recovery grain the catalog does not carry: a fresh run pointed at a prior crashed run's folder reuses that run's finished sub-run fanout branches by structural address (step_id, branch_id) instead of re-running them, without ever resuming the dead run (fresh-run only; explicitly rejected on resume at src/cli/run.ts:407-409). It falls between resume-work (whose summary is explicitly 'the same durable run', which this flag is barred from) and recover-cleanly (whose surfaces cover only resource reclamation and in-flow recovery blocks). Best fix at the catalog's grain: an extension relationship on recover-cleanly (not resume-work, since the mechanism mints a new run identity), or a note on recover-cleanly adding this as a bounded recovery path with proof refs src/runtime/run/reuse-children.ts and tests/runtime/reuse-children.test.ts (proof strength 'tested', exposure public-cli). confirmed_candidates.detail: Review runs exclude untracked file contents from what is sent to the configured worker unless the operator passes --include-untracked-content. The catalog's boundaries section lists four deliberate boundaries (bounded-dynamism, invoked-flows, no-keep-best-loop, authored-allocation) but has no data-scope/privacy boundary, even though this one is enforced fail-closed in the flag surface and is exactly the kind of deliberate limit the section exists to record.

No refutation ground fully lands: it is not covered elsewhere (role-shaped-steps is about fitting context to steps, not data egress), it exists on main, and the hard fence invites catalog edits. However, the candidate overclaims on grain in two ways. (1) 'Untracked file contents never leave the machine unless opted in' is not a product-wide invariant — enforcement lives only in Review's intake writer; workers in other flows have repo tool access and can read untracked files directly, and Review does relay tracked diff content by default. confirmed_candidates.title: Engine-enforced evidence integrity: overclaims and gamed proof cannot close a run
confirmed_candidates.detail: The engine actively verifies worker claims against ground truth and refuses to close when they fail: the honesty ledger latches overclaims (a relay that claimed changed files the working tree does not show) and makes a clean 'complete' impossible while any latch is open; the frozen-eval guard fingerprints the declared eval surface and refuses a goal-met claim after any tampering ('a tampered run can only ever end needs-attention, never complete'); the until-loop stop-judge boolean is DISPOSED against an independent evidence floor rather than trusted; and the bindsTerminalOutcomeToPrimaryResult engine flag downgrades an @complete close when the primary result carries a non-complete outcome. No catalog capability covers this. 'deterministic-checks' is running declared commands; 'independent-judgment' is a separate reviewer role; 'honest-close' is the close writer telling the truth about available evidence. None of them is the engine adversarially checking the worker's claims and structurally blocking false-done. This is the enforcement mechanism behind the proof-before-progress vision statement and the launch messaging's honesty floor, and it is invisible in the map.
confirmed_candidates.evidence: src/runtime/run/honesty-ledger.ts (overclaim latches + finalize chokepoint); src/runtime/run/frozen-eval.ts (eval-surface fingerprinting); src/flows/types.ts:135-165 (stopJudge disposal + needsAttentionRoute so exhaustion can never read as success) and 230-235 (bindsTerminalOutcomeToPrimaryResult); src/runtime/run/trace-evidence.ts

verdict.reasoning: All cited mechanisms exist, are committed clean on main, and are wired: honesty-ledger latches feed the finalize chokepoint at src/runtime/run/run-close.ts:326 (open latch blocks clean complete, downgrades to stopped); frozen-eval fingerprint guard is live on a cataloged flow (src/flows/sweep/assembly-spec.ts:231 sets frozen_paths); the stop-judge boolean is disposed against an independent evidence floor (src/runtime/run/until-corridor.ts) with a mandatory needsAttentionRoute that must target a non-@complete terminal (src/flows/types.ts:160-165); bindsTerminalOutcomeToPrimaryResult downgrades @complete closes (run-close.ts:106, armed by the review flow). Catalog read in full: no capability, boundary, or review question names engine-side verification of worker claims, and zero catalog refs reach src/runtime/run/ at all, so the enforcement machinery is genuinely invisible in the map. However, the candidate overstates by calling it a wholly missing capability: the outcomes are cataloged (honest-close's summary 'End with an outcome the available evidence supports' is exactly what the chokepoint and downgrade deliver; the ledger/stop-judge/frozen-eval machinery is the implementation of iterate-until-proof), and the catalog's grain is operator accomplishments, where a guarantee is arguably proof depth rather than a new entry. The sharpened, defensible finding is an attribution/coverage gap rather than a cleanly absent capability.
verdict.correction: Coverage gap (high): the catalog covers the honesty floor's outcomes but attributes them entirely to worker-side surfaces, hiding the engine-side enforcement that makes them guarantees. honest-close maps only worker-side close blocks (goal-close, close-with-evidence) and refs docs/contracts/run.md, which never mentions the latch/downgrade machinery; iterate-until-proof's summary ('while its authored condition says the proof is not yet sufficient') implies the judge is trusted, when the engine actually treats the judge's goal-met boolean as an untrusted proposal disposed against an independent evidence floor. The actual enforcement — honesty-ledger overclaim latches blocking clean complete at the run-close finalize chokepoint (src/runtime/run/run-close.ts:326), the frozen-eval fingerprint guard (live on sweep via frozen_paths), the stop-judge disposal with mandatory non-@complete needsAttentionRoute, and the bindsTerminalOutcomeToPrimaryResult downgrade — appears nowhere: no capability, boundary, review question, or ref reaches src/runtime/run/ at all. Since the honesty floor is one of three settled launch-messaging pillars and the enforcement of the proof-before-progress vision floor, an agent using this map cannot find what distinguishes Circuit's floor from a prompt-level convention. Fix: either add a guarantee-grain capability (engine-enforced evidence integrity, exposure mixed via converge-proof/fix-until-green/sweep/review) or strengthen honest-close and iterate-until-proof with proof refs to run-close.ts, honesty-ledger.ts, frozen-eval.ts, and until-corridor.ts plus attention notes naming the engine-side enforcement.
